cost_basis.cheapest_design: First compare adequate declared mechanisms: literal bands avoid inference calls but still incur execution and authoring cost; Jev is a candidate for bounded contextual estimates, not automatically more faithful. Q83 specifies varying inputs, fixed model context, interventions and applicability. Comparison is conditional on a named residual decision after argument; agreement cannot validate replacement (Q88). Worked historical blade-only component: 30 queries times $0.0000279 = $0.000837 before retries, excluding crossing-context calls and other work. Current-workload price, cache share and latency require their own basis. The 5-second-per-attempt design ceiling is conditional on actual enforcement; current service timeout policy does not establish it. Choosing Jev for a stopping classifier requires a separate Q86 adequacy decision, not sampling answer confidence.

plain_baseline.answer_path: Jev's estimate of a chance (later a pick or an amount) from the world's facts, used by an estimate rule
plain_baseline.when: Conditional diagnostic only: first name the backend or omitted-dependency decision that survives mechanism/intervention analysis under Q83, and the observation that would change it. No comparative run is authorized merely to satisfy this record. If needed, use the retained candidate set in docs/plans/estimate_rules.md.
cases: blade, 0 days since service after a failure, load 0

stage_effects.stage: declared varying inputs plus fixed model context under the Q83 mechanism/intervention contract
stage_effects.gap: An unauthorized or irrelevant context field can change an estimate and invalidate reuse. The design boundary is settled; backend adequacy under its declared applicability remains unproved. A comparison is a conditional diagnostic, not proof of sufficiency.

stage_effects.stage: per-run cache: resolved model, estimator/prompt version, question/type/options and read values (E1)
stage_effects.gap: not an answer-quality stage: it removes repeat calls with identical inputs; its effect on cost and time is measured in E1

stage_effects.stage: draw against the estimate instead of using the estimate as the outcome (E1)
stage_effects.gap: used directly, a probability becomes a truth claim (the retired Jev note's anti-pattern, 'P(fire)=0.81 -> fire=true'), so a world fails every day above a threshold and never below it; shown by argument, untested on a run until E1
